text:
Marta: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR to clean up Dedicated capacity SLA language and to add a short SDK example for isolation tags. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4328
Kai: Reviewing now. main ask: make the SLA table explicit about eviction vs preemption and what customers can expect under reserved capacity.
Marta: Exactly — the current wording is ambiguous about eviction during node reclamation vs tenant preemption. Want a short plain-language sentence plus the SLA table.
Ram: I can add an example autoscale policy snippet (YAML + terraform snippet) showing scaleToAverage and a burst window. Do we want both k8s and terraform examples?
Marta: Yes please both. Keep the k8s example tiny. Terraform should show reserved_pool and min/max.
Liam: Quick question: what should we call the eviction behavior in the text? "eviction" or "preemption"? Legal prefers "preemption" but eng uses "eviction".
Sophia: From docs POV, use "preemption (eviction)" first time, then "preemption" after. Helps both audiences.
Eve: FYI impact matrix lives in the runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-eviction. Link should be referenced in the SLA section.
DocsBot: link-checker failed on one of the PR links — reported broken anchor: docs/dedicated/#reserved-pools -> 404.
Kai: I'll fix the anchor and reword the SLA paragraph. For the SDK snippet, do we want Python sync or async?
Marta: Python sync + JS snippet would be great. Keep them <10 LOC.
Ram: Draft autoscale YAML (will paste as suggestion):
Ram: ```yaml
scalePolicy:
  type: target_utilization
  target: 0.7
  windowSeconds: 60
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
```
Ram: Terraform example (minimal):
Ram: ```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "prod" {
  name     = "prod-reserved"
  gpu_type = "a100"
  min_capacity = 2
  max_capacity = 20
  isolation = "tenant"
}
```
Marta: Nice. Can we call out that "isolation = \"tenant\"" implies dedicated scheduling and eviction protection semantics? Add a short note.
Kai: Will add this bullet: "tenant isolation: reserved nodes scheduled for a single tenant; preemption only in out-of-contract emergency; see runbook."
Liam: Also add a tiny table row in SLA summary: "Preemption: <1% monthly expected for reserved pools under normal ops" — placeholder numbers OK but mark as draft.
Sophia: I'll move SDK snippets to docs/examples/dedicated-sdk and add cross-links. Also will create an anchor for the runbook link to avoid the bot error.
Eve: Suggest adding an explicit rollback policy example for canary rollouts in Dedicated — small note under rollout section.
Marta: Agreed. Add a 2-line canary example: route 5% -> new model, fallback to previous on latency/error threshold.
Kai: One more: please ensure we don't promise latency SLOs for preemptible bursts in reserved pools. Add statement: "Latency SLOs apply to committed capacity; best-effort for burst".
Marta: Good call.
Ram: I'll push a follow-up commit with the terraform snippet and autoscale YAML.
Kai: I'm making wording changes now, will push to the PR and ping reviewers.
DocsBot: PR 4328 — status: changes requested (link-checks failing).
Marta: Thanks all. If anyone wants to pair on the SDK snippet wording ping me in threads. :thumbsup:
Sophia: I'll open a small follow-up PR for the example files after Kai lands wording changes.
Liam: LGTM for the structure. Quick note: add an explicit example showing request routing policy: latency-first vs cost-first (1 sentence).
Marta: Noted. I'll add routing policy blurb.
Eve: Added a comment in the PR about referencing the eviction runbook and the telemetry dashboard to verify preemption rates.
Kai: Done — pushed wording + fixed anchor. re-run checks.
DocsBot: link-checker passed. CI: docs-build passed.
Marta: Awesome, thanks! We'll merge after Sophia's example PR.
Sophia: Will aim to open it in ~1h.
Ram: PR follow-up incoming in ~30m with snippets.
Marta: Great teamwork.
